title: Danya VS Magnus
reviewNotes: Saved montage and captions reviewed with native complete board checks. Begin immediately after the illustrated h8=Q at 57 seconds in the complete eleven-piece later diagram. The finite mate certificate covers both White king replies to a2+ and every subsequent defense, retaining Ne5 and White e3/e4/f4/g2. The source knight-promotion and king-return queen-promotion branches are shown; the omitted Kc1/b2 mate is explicitly independent. The earlier Kc3 move and alternatives to h8=Q remain unverified context, not a claim that the original position was lost or that promotion was White’s only move.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only Daniel Naroditski would have been [music] able to defeat Magnus Carson himself from this position. During the pandemic, these two were playing an extremely long match of bullet games. In this position, it seems like white is completely winning, having three extra pawns, [music] and one of them is only one step away from getting a new queen. But Daniel's only two pawns, king and bishop, are very close to the white king. But unfortunately, if you simply try to [music] push these pawns, there is not going to be any promotion. The white king is simply going to pick this up. And now this is forever defended. And the same thing goes for B2. But with only 10 seconds left on the clock in this position, Da found an [music] incredible resource that even Magnus Carlson himself missed and he played king [music] to C3. Now, this doesn't really seem to achieve anything. So, the goat simply promoted to a new queen, thinking that he would [music] simply win this. But actually this is a blunder and believe it or not white is already [music] lost in this position. Black follows up with A2 check and of course the king goes to the corner. The at the time war chess champion for sure calculated this and saw no danger. But Grandmaster Daniel followed up with B2 [music] check now sacrificing the A2 pawn. What is possibly the idea here? If black promotes this is simply going to get captured by the king and white is simply out of the woods. But there is the very precise intermetzo bishop b3 [music] check. Now this forces white to make a choice to either go back to b1 or to go up to a3. If the king goes back now this is simple. We're going to follow up with bishop to c2 check. The only move is to go back and now after the queen promotes with check. The king is forced here and this is [music] going to be checkmate. But what Magnus had calculated in those couple of seconds was that he was simply going to go up. And now after you get a queen, this is not a check. And so he could have started attacking the [music] black king and win thanks to his four extra pawns. But here with only a couple of seconds left on the clock, Grandmaster Daniel Naiski promoted anyway but to a knight [music] and delivered this brilliant knight and bishop checkmate. Never forget da.
